references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the man with the withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath, where Jesus heals him.
Mark's parallel account of the man with the withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath, which is the closest parallel to Luke's narrative.
Jesus entered the synagogue in Capernaum and taught on the Sabbath, showing his habit of teaching in the synagogue on the Sabbath day.
The immediately preceding pericope about the disciples picking grain on the Sabbath, which together with the healing in verses 6–11 forms a pair of Sabbath controversy stories.
Another incident where Jesus heals in the synagogue on the Sabbath—the woman who had been bent over for eighteen years—and the synagogue leader reacts with anger.
Yet another Sabbath healing where Jesus challenges the Pharisees' attitude toward healing on the Sabbath, this time with a man suffering from dropsy.
Jeroboam's hand withered when he reached out against the prophet, and God healed it again—an Old Testament example of a withered hand being restored.
Jesus entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day, as was his custom, which sets the background for him also entering the synagogue in 6:6 on a Sabbath to teach.
